selah-and-the-spades.d: At an elite Pennsylvania boarding school, a senior who commands one of five underground student factions grooms a freshman protégé to inherit her power while her own carefully built world begins to fracture.

cane-river.d: A romance across Louisiana's Creole class lines between a Black-identified young man and a lighter-skinned Creole woman from a family that has long denied its African ancestry; unseen for over 30 years before its rediscovery and restoration.

charm-city-kings.d: A fourteen-year-old in Baltimore is drawn into the city's real-life dirt-bike riding crews, torn between the family that took him under its wing and the dangerous street life that surrounds it.

monster-s-ball.d: A grieving widow and the racist corrections officer connected to her husband's execution form an unlikely, redemptive relationship in the rural South. Halle Berry won the Academy Award for Best Actress for the role.

down-in-the-delta.d: A struggling Chicago mother is sent by her own mother to spend the summer with relatives in the Mississippi Delta, where reconnecting with her family's roots helps her rebuild her life. The only feature directed by Maya Angelou.

their-eyes-were-watching-god.d: An adaptation of Zora Neale Hurston's novel following Janie Crawford through three marriages in the early-20th-century South as she searches for love and self-determination.

american-violet.d: Based on a true story: a single mother in a small Texas town fights to clear her name after being wrongfully swept up in a racially charged drug bust and pressured to plead guilty to a crime she didn't commit.

night-catches-us.d: In 1976 Philadelphia, a former Black Panther returns home for his father's funeral and rekindles a bond with the widow of a slain comrade, stirring up old suspicions and unresolved violence from the movement's collapse.

kicks.d: A Bay Area teen scrapes together enough money for the sneakers he's always wanted, only to have them stolen at gunpoint, sending him and his friends on a dangerous quest through Oakland to get them back.

newlyweeds.d: A Brooklyn couple's shared love of marijuana starts to unravel their relationship and jobs as their habit spirals, in the feature debut of Judas and the Black Messiah director Shaka King.

medicine-for-melancholy.d: After a one-night stand, two young Black San Franciscans spend the following day together, drifting through the city and debating identity, gentrification, and whether to see each other again. Barry Jenkins' feature debut.

blue-caprice.d: A fictionalized account of the relationship between John Allen Muhammad and the teenage Lee Boyd Malvo, tracing how a father figure radicalized a vulnerable boy into carrying out the 2002 D.C. sniper attacks.

night-of-the-kings.d: A new inmate at an inmate-ruled Ivorian prison is forced by tradition to entertain the other prisoners by telling a story that must last until dawn, or face death, blending myth and modern gang history.

rafiki.d: In Nairobi, two young women from rival political families fall in love despite a society and legal system that criminalizes their relationship, becoming the first Kenyan film to premiere at Cannes.

timbuktu.d: A cattle herder and his family living outside a jihadist-occupied Malian city try to preserve a quiet, ordinary life as the militants impose brutal edicts on the town's residents.

tsotsi.d: A young gang leader in a Johannesburg slum steals a car and discovers an infant in the backseat, an accident that forces him to confront the violence of his own life. Winner of the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

sarafina.d: A musical drama set during the 1976 Soweto Uprising, following a Black South African schoolgirl inspired by her teacher to join student protests against apartheid education policy.

cry-freedom.d: The true story of the friendship between South African anti-apartheid activist Steve Biko and journalist Donald Woods, and Woods' dangerous escape after Biko's death in police custody. Denzel Washington earned an Oscar nomination as Biko.

catch-a-fire.d: A true story of an apolitical South African oil refinery worker who, after being wrongfully tortured by security police as a terrorism suspect, becomes radicalized and joins the armed anti-apartheid resistance.

sometimes-in-april.d: A former Hutu army officer, haunted by his brother's role inciting the 1994 Rwandan genocide, returns to Kigali years later to confront his past and search for the family he was separated from during the massacre.

trading-places.d: A wealthy commodities broker and a street hustler are used as unwitting pawns in a bet by two rich brothers, swapping their fortunes and social positions overnight.

beverly-hills-cop.d: Detroit cop Axel Foley travels to Beverly Hills to investigate a friend's murder, clashing with the local police department's by-the-book style along the way.

48-hrs.d: A San Francisco cop springs a wisecracking convict from prison for 48 hours to help him track down two cop killers.

the-golden-child.d: A social worker specializing in finding missing children is recruited to rescue a mystical Tibetan child kidnapped by a demonic sorcerer.

doctor-dolittle.d: A San Francisco physician discovers he has the ability to talk to animals, who begin lining up for house calls and pull him into their world.

dr-dolittle-2.d: Dr. Dolittle is enlisted by forest animals to help a clumsy circus bear learn to survive in the wild so a threatened woodland can be saved from developers.

life.d: Two men wrongly convicted of murder in 1930s Mississippi spend decades together on a Southern prison farm, their friendship enduring across a lifetime.

daddy-day-care.d: Two laid-off marketing executives open their own home day care center, competing against a snobbish, high-priced rival institution.

norbit.d: A meek man trapped in a miserable marriage to his domineering wife reconnects with his childhood sweetheart and must find the courage to change his life.

meet-dave.d: A tiny alien crew pilots a human-shaped ship called Dave on a mission to Earth, where their captain falls for a local woman and starts to question his orders.

imagine-that.d: A workaholic financial executive discovers his young daughter's imaginary world holds surprisingly accurate business tips, forcing him to reconnect with her.

mo-money.d: A small-time hustler and his brother scheme their way into jobs at a credit card company, uncovering a bigger fraud operation while chasing a woman he's fallen for.

major-payne.d: A hard-nosed, decorated Marine major is reassigned to whip an unruly college ROTC cadet unit into shape, using tactics far too extreme for campus life.

blankman.d: An eccentric inventor from a crime-ridden neighborhood builds his own gadgets and costume to become a bumbling but well-meaning superhero.

juwanna-mann.d: A suspended, arrogant men's basketball star disguises himself as a woman to join a women's professional league, learning humility and teamwork along the way.

kingdom-come.d: A dysfunctional Black family reunites for the funeral of their harsh, unloved patriarch, and old grievances boil over during the wake.

like-mike.d: An orphan boy finds a pair of old sneakers stamped with the initials 'MJ' that, after a lightning strike, give him the ability to play basketball like a pro.

nutty-professor-ii-the-klumps.d: Professor Sherman Klump proposes to his girlfriend while his alter ego Buddy Love, extracted as his own being, schemes to sabotage the relationship.

beauty-shop.d: A talented hairstylist quits her upscale salon job to open her own shop, assembling a colorful staff and battling her old boss for clients.

soul-plane.d: After winning a lawsuit against an airline, a man launches his own hip-hop-themed airline, leading to a chaotic maiden flight full of mishaps.

mr-3000.d: A retired, self-centered baseball star discovers a scorekeeping error means he's short of his career hit milestone and returns to the game at 47 to reach it.

johnson-family-vacation.d: A separated family piles into an RV for a cross-country road trip to a family reunion, hitting one comic disaster after another along the way.

are-we-there-yet.d: A bachelor trying to win over a divorced woman ends up driving her two mischievous kids across several states, who do everything they can to sabotage the trip.

are-we-done-yet.d: Now married with a baby on the way, a man moves his blended family to a fixer-upper house in the country, where renovation chaos ensues.

guess-who.d: An overprotective father meets his daughter's white fiancé for the first time over a tense family weekend, a comic inversion of Guess Who's Coming to Dinner.

woo.d: A free-spirited, unpredictable woman drags her blind date, a shy paralegal, through one bizarre calamity after another across a single wild night out.

something-new.d: A driven Black accountant reluctantly falls for the white landscape architect she hires, upending the plans she'd made for the kind of man and life she wanted.

baggage-claim.d: A flight attendant facing her younger sister's wedding gives herself 30 days and unlimited air miles to find a fiancé among her past boyfriends.

the-perfect-holiday.d: A struggling songwriter working as a mall Santa hears a single mother's daughter wish for her mom to find love, and sets out to make it happen himself.

this-christmas.d: The adult Whitfield siblings gather at their mother's house for their first Christmas together in years, and long-buried family secrets surface over the holiday.

frank-s-place.d: A Boston professor inherits his late father's New Orleans restaurant, Chez Louisiane, and stays on to run it, immersing himself in the city's Creole culture and colorful regulars.

the-royal-family.d: Executive produced by Eddie Murphy, this CBS sitcom followed retired mailman Al Royal and his wife Victoria as their adult daughter and grandchildren move back in with them.

under-one-roof.d: Three generations of the Langston family share a two-family house in Seattle, led by widowed police-officer patriarch Neb, who has taken in a troubled foster son.

the-parent-hood.d: A former English professor becomes a hands-on father to his four kids in Harlem after his lawyer wife returns to work.

malcolm-and-eddie.d: Responsible convenience-store manager Malcolm and fast-talking tow-truck owner Eddie end up as roommates and business partners in Kansas City.

the-hughleys.d: Comedian D.L. Hughley co-created and stars as Darryl Hughley, who moves his family from the inner city to a mostly white suburb of Los Angeles.

eve.d: Rapper Eve stars as a Miami fashion designer navigating friendship and relationships alongside her girlfriends and a trio of guy friends.

soul-food-2.d: Adapted from the 1997 film, this Showtime drama follows the Josephs, a tight-knit Chicago family, through love, loss and rivalry over five seasons.

real-husbands-of-hollywood.d: A Real Housewives-style scripted parody in which Kevin Hart and a circle of celebrity friends play fictionalized versions of themselves navigating Hollywood marriages and egos.

are-we-there-yet-2.d: Based on the Ice Cube film, this TBS sitcom follows newlyweds Nick and Suzanne blending their families and navigating stepparenthood.

the-carmichael-show.d: A fictionalized version of comedian Jerrod Carmichael's Charlotte family tackles hot-button social topics head-on in front of a live studio audience.

mixed-ish.d: A prequel to black-ish, this ABC sitcom follows Rainbow Johnson's childhood in the 1980s as her mixed-race family leaves a hippie commune to adjust to suburban life.

rel.d: Loosely based on Lil Rel Howery's own life, a Chicago man tries to rebuild after discovering his ex-wife slept with his barber.

sherman-s-showcase.d: A mockumentary parody of long-running Black music variety shows like Soul Train, centered on the fictional longtime host and producer of a musical variety program.

woke.d: A Black cartoonist on the verge of mainstream success has his worldview upended after a run-in with police, and starts hallucinating talking inanimate objects that push him toward political awakening.

truth-be-told.d: True-crime podcaster Poppy Parnell revisits the case that made her famous, digging back into a wrongful-conviction story and the family it shattered.

the-porter.d: Set in 1920s Montreal and Chicago, this drama dramatizes the true story of Black railway porters who organized North America's first Black labor union.

61st-street.d: A Chicago defense attorney nearing retirement takes on the case of a young Black man wrongly accused of killing a police officer, exposing the city's fractured justice system.

first-wives-club.d: Three women who band together after their marriages fall apart find sisterhood, revenge and reinvention in Atlanta.

diarra-from-detroit.d: A recently divorced Detroit schoolteacher believes she's been ghosted by her rebound Tinder date and launches her own amateur investigation, pulling her into the city's underworld.

all-american-homecoming.d: A spin-off of All American following a tennis phenom who enrolls at a historically Black university, chasing her dream while confronting family secrets.

power-book-iv-force.d: Power fan-favorite Tommy Egan leaves New York for Chicago and sets out to build his own drug empire from scratch, clashing with the city's entrenched crews.

the-neighborhood.d: A white Midwestern family moves into a predominantly Black Pasadena neighborhood, and the two families next door become unlikely friends.

charlie-and-co.d: A middle-class Chicago highway-department employee and his schoolteacher wife raise three kids in this CBS family sitcom, seen at the time as CBS's answer to The Cosby Show.

grady.d: A spin-off of Sanford and Son, following Fred Sanford's widower friend Grady Wilson as he leaves Watts to move in with his daughter's family in Westwood.

tongues-untied.d: A landmark experimental documentary exploring the lives, identities, and struggles of Black gay men in America through poetry, testimony, and personal reflection.

ethnic-notions.d: A history of deeply rooted anti-Black stereotypes in American popular culture, tracing caricatures like Sambo, Mammy, and the minstrel through more than a century of media.

paris-is-burning.d: A vivid chronicle of New York City's Black and Latino drag ball culture in the 1980s, capturing the voguing scene and the chosen 'houses' that sustained its LGBTQ community.

freedom-riders.d: The story of the interracial groups of young activists who rode buses into the segregated South in 1961 to challenge Jim Crow travel laws, facing mob violence and imprisonment.

the-loving-story.d: Using rare archival footage, this documentary tells the story of Richard and Mildred Loving, whose interracial marriage led to the landmark Supreme Court case Loving v. Virginia.

toni-morrison-the-pieces-i-am.t: Toni Morrison: The Pieces I Am
toni-morrison-the-pieces-i-am.d: An intimate look at the life and career of Nobel laureate Toni Morrison, tracing her literary journey and her lasting influence on American letters and Black identity.

sammy-davis-jr-i-ve-gotta-be-me.t: Sammy Davis, Jr.: I've Gotta Be Me
sammy-davis-jr-i-ve-gotta-be-me.d: A comprehensive American Masters portrait of entertainer Sammy Davis Jr., tracing his rise from a child vaudeville star to a groundbreaking multi-hyphenate performer navigating race in show business.

whitney.d: An unflinching, fully authorized documentary examining the life, career, and struggles of singer Whitney Houston, drawing on unseen footage and candid family interviews.

miles-davis-birth-of-the-cool.t: Miles Davis: Birth of the Cool
miles-davis-birth-of-the-cool.d: An American Masters documentary tracing jazz icon Miles Davis's evolution across decades of musical reinvention, drawing on his own words and those who knew him best.

american-promise.d: Filmmakers Joe Brewster and Michèle Stephenson document their son's and his best friend's 13-year journey through an elite private school, exploring race, education, and Black boyhood in America.

muhammad-ali.d: A four-part Ken Burns docuseries tracing boxing legend Muhammad Ali's life from his Louisville upbringing through his championship career, activism, and later years.

chisholm-72-unbought-and-unbossed.d: A documentary portrait of Shirley Chisholm's historic 1972 campaign to become the first Black woman to run for a major party's presidential nomination.

the-central-park-five.d: Ken Burns, Sarah Burns, and David McMahon document the wrongful conviction of five Black and Latino teenagers for a 1989 Central Park assault, exposing a rush to judgment fueled by racial bias.

slavery-by-another-name.d: Based on Douglas Blackmon's Pulitzer-winning book, this PBS documentary reveals how forced Black labor persisted through convict leasing and debt peonage long after the Emancipation Proclamation.

two-trains-runnin.d: Narrated by Common, this documentary follows two groups of young music fans searching for forgotten blues legends Skip James and Son House in Mississippi during Freedom Summer 1964.

tell-them-we-are-rising-the-story-of-bla.t: Tell Them We Are Rising: The Story of Black Colleges and Universities
tell-them-we-are-rising-the-story-of-bla.d: A sweeping history of Historically Black Colleges and Universities and their role in shaping American education, culture, and the fight for civil rights.

la-92.d: A visceral, archival-footage-only account of the 1992 Los Angeles riots that erupted after the acquittal of the police officers who beat Rodney King.

amandla-a-revolution-in-four-part-harmon.t: Amandla! A Revolution in Four-Part Harmony
amandla-a-revolution-in-four-part-harmon.d: A chronological history of South Africa's anti-apartheid struggle told through the freedom songs that fueled and united the movement.

the-black-power-mixtape-1967-1975.d: Built from newly unearthed 16mm footage shot by Swedish journalists, this documentary revisits the Black Power movement through its key figures and contemporary musical commentary.

say-amen-somebody.d: A joyous documentary on the history of American gospel music told through the lives of pioneers Thomas A. Dorsey and 'Mother' Willie Mae Ford Smith.

the-nine-lives-of-marion-barry.t: The Nine Lives of Marion Barry
the-nine-lives-of-marion-barry.d: An HBO documentary chronicling the rise, fall, and political comebacks of Marion Barry, the civil-rights-activist-turned-mayor of Washington, D.C.

soundtrack-for-a-revolution.d: The story of the American Civil Rights Movement told through the freedom songs that sustained activists, paired with new performances by contemporary artists.

faubourg-trem-the-untold-story-of-black-.t: Faubourg Tremé: The Untold Story of Black New Orleans
faubourg-trem-the-untold-story-of-black-.d: A history of New Orleans's Tremé neighborhood, the oldest Black neighborhood in America and a cradle of jazz and Southern civil rights activism.

citizen-king.d: An American Experience documentary examining the final, more turbulent five years of Martin Luther King Jr.'s life and activism, from the March on Washington to his assassination.

the-murder-of-fred-hampton.d: Originally filmed as a portrait of the Illinois Black Panther Party, this documentary became an investigation into the 1969 police killing of its young chairman, Fred Hampton.

citation.d: A university student in Nigeria speaks out after a charismatic visiting professor sexually assaults her, and must fight the institution's reluctance to hold him accountable.

king-of-boys.d: A powerful Lagos businesswoman and philanthropist with a hidden criminal past pursues political ambition, dragging her into a power struggle that threatens her family and empire.

the-milkmaid.d: A Fulani milkmaid searches for her younger sister after religious extremists tear their family apart, forcing her into painful compromises to reclaim what she's lost.

lionheart.d: When her father falls ill, a young woman steps up alongside her eccentric uncle to save the family transport company from financial ruin.

anikulapo.d: A traveling weaver in the old Oyo kingdom begins an illicit affair with the king's wife, an entanglement that leads to his death and a fateful encounter with a mystical bird that can restore life.

gangs-of-lagos.d: Three childhood friends raised in a politically-controlled Lagos neighborhood get pulled into escalating gang warfare as rival factions fight for territory.

blue-story.d: Two best friends from rival South London neighborhoods are driven apart and into a violent postcode gang war, narrated in rap by writer-director Rapman.

farming.d: Based on the director's own childhood, a Nigerian boy fostered by a white working-class family in 1980s Essex grows up to join a white skinhead gang.

the-wedding-party.d: A lavish Lagos wedding between two families spirals into chaos as clashing personalities, secrets, and last-minute scandal threaten to derail the big day.

isoken.d: A successful but single 34-year-old woman faces family pressure to marry a suitable Edo man, but instead finds herself falling for a white British suitor.

rocks.d: A Black British teenager in Hackney is forced to care for her younger brother after their mother abandons them, leaning on friendship and resilience to survive.

boxing-day.d: A British writer brings his American fiancée home to London for the holidays, only to find his ex-girlfriend still part of the family orbit, in the UK's first Black-led Christmas rom-com.

sprinter.d: A gifted Jamaican teen sprinter hopes his rise in track and field will reunite him with the mother who has lived undocumented in the U.S. for over a decade.

yardie.d: A young Jamaican man sent to broker a drug deal in 1980s London instead crosses paths with the man who killed his brother, spiraling into violence and betrayal.

play-the-devil.d: A gifted young man from a poor Trinidad village begins a secret affair with an older, wealthy benefactor, culminating at Carnival's devil dance.

the-burial-of-kojo.d: A young Ghanaian girl travels through a mystical spirit realm to save her father, left to die in an abandoned gold mine, in a story recounted by her older self.

swallow.d: In 1980s Lagos, a naive young secretary is drawn into drug smuggling by her streetwise roommate after a string of career failures, with dangerous consequences.

sew-the-winter-to-my-skin.t: Sew the Winter to My Skin
sew-the-winter-to-my-skin.d: Based on real events, an African folk hero steals from wealthy white landowners to give to the poor in 1950s apartheid-era South Africa, sparking a nationwide manhunt.

knuckle-city.d: An aging South African boxer, haunted by his father's legacy, attempts a comeback fight to pull his family out of poverty and crime.

been-so-long.d: A single mother working at a hair salon in multicultural Camden Town finds an unexpected romance in this British stage-musical adaptation shot through with song.

second-coming.d: A London woman's unexplained pregnancy, despite months without intimacy with her husband or anyone else, slowly fractures her tight-knit family.

kingston-paradise.d: A small-time Kingston hustler and his roommate, a sex worker, dream of escaping their tenement life via a risky car-theft scheme, with devastating fallout.

chief-daddy.d: A wealthy Lagos industrialist's sudden death sets off a chaotic scramble among his sprawling extended family, staff, and mistresses over his will.

pumzi.d: In a drought-ravaged future East Africa, a museum curator defies an authoritarian council to plant a germinating seed in the derelict outside world. Short film that premiered at Sundance.

when-we-were-kings.d: Academy Award-winning documentary chronicling the 1974 'Rumble in the Jungle' heavyweight title fight between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in Kinshasa, Zaire, and the cultural spectacle surrounding it.

undefeated.d: Oscar-winning documentary following the underfunded Manassas High School football team in North Memphis and volunteer coach Bill Courtney's push for the program's first playoff win in over a century.

benji.d: ESPN 30 for 30 documentary on Chicago basketball phenom Ben 'Benji' Wilson, the nation's top-ranked high school player, whose 1984 murder became a turning point in the city's conversation about youth violence.

the-fab-five.d: ESPN 30 for 30 documentary on Michigan's freshman-heavy 1991 basketball recruiting class, whose baggy shorts, black socks, and swagger changed college basketball culture and reached back-to-back title games.

doc-and-darryl.d: ESPN 30 for 30 documentary on 1986 Mets stars Dwight Gooden and Darryl Strawberry, whose dazzling talent and intertwined careers were derailed by addiction, told through their decades-long friendship.

bad-boys.d: ESPN 30 for 30 documentary on the late-1980s/early-90s Detroit Pistons, whose physical, defense-first style and back-to-back championships made them the league's most feared and reviled team.

the-announcement.d: ESPN Films documentary revisiting Magic Johnson's stunning 1991 announcement that he had contracted HIV, and how he redefined public understanding of the disease while fighting to return to the NBA.

marion-jones-press-pause.d: ESPN 30 for 30 documentary directed by John Singleton examining sprinter Marion Jones's five-medal performance at the 2000 Sydney Olympics and her fall from grace after admitting to steroid use.

the-best-that-never-was.d: ESPN 30 for 30 documentary on Marcus Dupree, a running back phenom from Philadelphia, Mississippi, whose electrifying talent made him the nation's most recruited player before injuries derailed his path to stardom.

through-the-fire.d: HBO documentary following Brooklyn point guard Sebastian Telfair through his senior year of high school as he navigates fame, family expectations, and the leap straight to the NBA.

facing-ali.d: Documentary told through the eyes of ten of Muhammad Ali's opponents, reflecting on what it meant to share the ring with the man who redefined boxing and Black self-assertion.

i-am-ali.d: Documentary built around Muhammad Ali's personal audio diaries, interwoven with interviews from his family, friends, and fellow fighters.

what-s-my-name-muhammad-ali.d: HBO two-part documentary told almost entirely through archival footage and Ali's own words, covering his boxing career, his refusal of the Vietnam draft, and his role as a global icon of Black pride.

fists-of-freedom-the-story-of-the-68-sum.t: Fists of Freedom: The Story of the '68 Summer Games
fists-of-freedom-the-story-of-the-68-sum.d: HBO Sports documentary revisiting the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, centered on Tommie Smith and John Carlos's raised-fist Black Power salute on the medal stand and the fallout it triggered.

shut-up-and-dribble.d: Showtime docuseries executive produced by LeBron James tracing the modern NBA's evolution from the league's control of players' images to today's athletes wielding their platforms for social and political activism.

simone-biles-rising.d: Netflix docuseries following gymnast Simone Biles's mental-health-driven withdrawal from the Tokyo Olympics and her comeback culminating at the 2024 Paris Games.

michael-che-matters.d: SNL Weekend Update anchor Michael Che's debut Netflix stand-up special, tackling police brutality, race, and politics with blunt, controversy-courting jokes.

josh-johnson-up-here-killing-myself.t: Josh Johnson: Up Here Killing Myself
josh-johnson-up-here-killing-myself.d: Peacock stand-up special in which comedian and former Daily Show writer Josh Johnson frames his set around a therapy session, digging into Black mental health, grief, and growing up broke.

ali-siddiq-it-s-bigger-than-these-bars.t: Ali Siddiq: It's Bigger Than These Bars
ali-siddiq-it-s-bigger-than-these-bars.d: Comedy Central stand-up special filmed inside Bell County Jail in Belton, Texas, where former inmate Ali Siddiq performs storytelling-driven comedy about his years incarcerated for drug trafficking.

damon-wayans-the-last-stand.d: Showtime stand-up special from In Living Color creator Damon Wayans, mixing sharp social commentary with reflections on aging and fame.

jay-pharoah-can-i-be-me.t: Jay Pharoah: Can I Be Me?
jay-pharoah-can-i-be-me.d: Showtime debut stand-up special from former SNL cast member Jay Pharoah, blending celebrity impressions with personal stand-up material.

good-burger.d: Two employees of a struggling fast-food joint scramble to save it from a slick mega-chain that just opened across the street.

good-burger-2.d: Ed and Dexter reunite years later to fend off a corporate rival building a chain of burger-serving robots that threatens the original Good Burger.

don-t-be-a-menace-to-south-central-while.t: Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood
don-t-be-a-menace-to-south-central-while.d: A wide-eyed teen moves in with his cousin in South Central L.A. and gets a crash course in every early-90s 'hood movie cliché, in this rapid-fire Wayans Brothers parody.

booty-call.d: Two friends' double date spirals into an all-night odyssey across New York City after a simple condom run goes hilariously wrong.

the-brothers.d: Four lifelong Black male friends confront their own fears about love and commitment when one of them gets engaged.

mr-church.d: A gifted cook hired to care for a dying woman and her young daughter stays on for decades, becoming the family the girl never expected.

pride.d: Based on a true story: struggling to keep kids off the streets, Jim Ellis builds Philadelphia's first all-Black swim team in the face of segregation-era prejudice.

the-best-of-enemies.d: Based on a true story: civil rights activist Ann Atwater and a KKK leader are forced to co-chair a fraught 1971 summit on school desegregation in Durham, North Carolina.

cross.d: DC forensic psychologist and homicide detective Alex Cross hunts serial killers while fighting to protect his own family, adapted from James Patterson's novels.

lioness.d: A CIA task force recruits and trains undercover female operatives — 'Lionesses' — to infiltrate terror networks from the inside, led by veteran officer Joe McNamara.

paradise.d: Three years after a doomsday event, Secret Service agent Xavier Collins investigates the murder of the U.S. president inside a city-sized underground bunker, uncovering a conspiracy that puts him at odds with the bunker's powerful leader.

lanterns.d: New recruit John Stewart and Lantern legend Hal Jordan — two intergalactic cops — are pulled into a dark, earth-bound murder mystery in the American heartland. Aaron Pierre steps into the Green Lantern a whole generation grew up on. Eight episodes from Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof and Tom King.

fightland.d: On the night Duke Kilroy takes the world heavyweight title, an assault leaves his brother dead and lands him in prison. Eight years later he comes home for revenge on the kingpin who set him up — a British-set boxing crime drama executive produced by 50 Cent.

the-odyssey-2026.d: Christopher Nolan’s IMAX-shot telling of Homer’s epic — Odysseus, king of Ithaca, claws his way home across a decade of gods and monsters after the Trojan War. Lupita Nyong’o plays Helen and Clytemnestra, Zendaya is the goddess Athena, and Corey Hawkins appears as Polybus.

captain-america-brave-new-world-2025.d: After meeting with newly elected U.S. President Thaddeus Ross, Sam finds himself in the middle of an international incident. He must discover the reason behind a nefarious global plot before the true mastermind has the entire world seeing red.

g20-2025.d: After the G20 Summit is overtaken by terrorists, President Danielle Sutton must bring all her statecraft and military experience to defend her family and her fellow leaders.

the-woman-in-the-yard-2025.d: In the aftermath of her husband's death, widow Ramona's struggle to raise her two kids is hindered by the arrival of a mysterious woman with supernatural abilities.

40-acres-2025.d: Hailey Freeman and her family are the last descendants of African American farmers who settled in rural Canada after the Civil War. In a famine-decimated near future, they now struggle to safeguard their farm, as they make one last stand against a vicious militia hell-bent on taking their 40 Acres.

the-man-in-my-basement-2025.d: Down on his luck, Charles Blakey agrees to rent his basement to a mysterious stranger, unaware he may be letting in a force much darker than he imagined.
